title: Sweater pattern template
description: Reusable Markdown template for writing and sharing knit or crochet sweater patterns with sections for sizing, gauge, materials, construction type, and step-by-step directions
---

Use this reusable template to write and share your knit or crochet sweater patterns in Markdown. Fill in the bracketed sections with your pattern details. This template works for pullovers, cardigans, and top-down or bottom-up constructions.

**Related guides:** [Garment measurements](/reference/garment-measurements/), [Repeats and sizing](/style guide/sizing/), [Gauge](/style guide/gauge/), [Abbreviations](/style guide/abbreviations/)

## Pattern Instructions

### Collar / Neckline

**Option 1: Ribbing first (simpler)**
After casting on, work in 1x1 rib for [N] in/cm on smaller needles. Switch to larger needles and proceed.

**Option 2: Ribbing last (more structured)**
After casting on, switch to larger needles, knit one round, and proceed. Ribbing is picked up and worked after the body and sleeves are complete.

```plaintext
CO [N] sts using [cast-on method]. Place BOR marker and join for working in the round.
Work [N] rounds in [ribbing pattern].
```

### Yoke

```plaintext
[Increase round instructions with raglan marker placement]
[Increase every-N round until yoke depth reaches specified measurement]
```

**Marker set-up:** [k2, pN, k2, PM, kN, PM] twice. The 4 raglan markers separate right sleeve, front, left sleeve, and back sections.

**Design feature:** [e.g., The central N sts in the sleeve sections form a garter panel — knit 1 round, purl 1 round]

**Increase round:** [kfb, knit to 2 sts before raglan marker, kfb, k1, SM] 4 times [8 sts inc]

**Work even round:** [Knit to garter panel, work design feature, knit to marker, SM, knit to marker, SM] twice

Work increase rounds a total of [N] times. For larger sizes, switch to alternate increase patterns when sleeve sts reach [N] sts.

**[Diagram or schematic image showing yoke, sleeve separation, body, sleeves]**

### Check yoke depth

Work even (no further increases, continuing design feature) until yoke measures [N] in/cm deep, measured from cast-on at the front of the sweater.

### Short row shaping (optional)

Short rows raise the back neckline relative to the front for a better fit. Instructions are for German short rows; substitute your preferred method.

```plaintext
[German short row instructions]
Place CB marker. Short rows are worked symmetrically around centre back.
```

### Separate body and sleeves

```plaintext
Place [N] sleeve sts on hold on waste yarn.
Cast on [N] sts at underarm using backwards loop method.
Knit across front sts.
Place second sleeve sts on hold.
Cast on [N] sts at underarm.
Knit across back sts.
[N total body sts on needles]
```

### Body

Work in [main stitch pattern / stockinette] until body measures [N] in/cm from underarm, or [N] in/cm short of desired length.

**Length options:** [Two body length options; e.g., cropped and regular]

Switch to smaller needles and work [ribbing pattern] for [N] in/cm. Bind off all sts loosely.

### Sleeves

Place held sts back on larger needles. Pick up and knit [N] sts from underarm cast-on, knit around sleeve sts, pick up and knit [N] more sts from underarm. Place BOR marker.

**[Sleeve length option, e.g., Short / 3/4 / Long]**

```plaintext
[Decrease round instructions if applicable]
[Work even / decrease schedule until sleeve measures desired length]
```

Switch to smaller needles and work [ribbing pattern] for [N] in/cm. Bind off all sts loosely.

### Neckline ribbing (if worked last)

Using smaller needles, pick up and knit one st in each cast-on st. [N sts]. Join for working in the round.

Work in 1x1 rib for [N] in/cm. Bind off all sts loosely.
